correctness.rationale: A uniformly chosen point from a cycle of length k has probability k times the cycle multiplicity divided by M; therefore its mean and variance are S2/M and S3/M-(S2/M)^2. At fixed M the pair equals iff (S2,S3) equals. The exact coefficient recurrence C_k(m,u,v)=C_(k-1)(m,u,v)+C_k(m-k,u-k²,v-k³) exhausts all partitions of each m≤14, and a separate descending-part generator reproduces every coefficient. Through thirteen there are no collisions, at fourteen there is exactly one double fiber (74,434) arising from (7,4,3) and (6,6,1,1), and the two least-period supports are disjoint. Adding M-14 singleton cycles for every M≥14 produces equal moments by algebraic identity. Only the finite census uses computation; the infinite family is proven symbolically.

value.rationale: The support and count of primitive periodic orbits are central dynamical descriptors, while sampling a random state yields readily measurable least-period mean and variance. The theorem identifies the exact smallest population size at which these two natural observations lose all ability to reconstruct the unique cycle structure, including a uniquely minimal witness with disjoint period supports and an exact extension to all greater sizes. The small cutoff is natural and complete, not an arbitrary slice or routine numerical instance.
